chapters.category: Greek and Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 24 — The Seven Mountains and the Fragrant Tree
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic wording has been identified for 1 Enoch 24. The Greek Codex Panopolitanus (Cairo Papyrus 10759) preserves the complete six-verse chapter and is the translation base. The chapter's description of seven glorious mountains, the throne-like central height and the uniquely fragrant tree is rendered directly from that Greek text, without identifying the unnamed precious stones or tree beyond what the witness states. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: From there I journeyed to another place on the earth, and he showed me a mountain of fire that burned day and night.
verses.study: The journey moves from the westward running fire to a fiery mountain. Its continual burning links it with the unceasing motion of Chapter 23, but this time the fire marks a fixed landscape that Enoch must pass before seeing the seven glorious mountains.
crossReferences: Exodus 19:18 — Sinai burns with fire when the LORD descends
Deuteronomy 4:11 — the mountain burns with fire into the heart of heaven
Daniel 7:9–10 — fire surrounds the heavenly throne and court
1 Enoch 23:2–4 — an unceasing fire follows the course of the heavenly lights

verses.text: I passed beyond it and saw seven glorious mountains, each different from the others. Their stones were precious in beauty, and all the mountains were precious, glorious and splendid in appearance. Three were set toward the east, one beside another, and three toward the south, one beside another; and there were deep, rugged ravines, none of them joining another.
verses.study: The seven mountains combine ordered placement with striking variety. Precious stone, beauty and glory distinguish them, while deep ravines keep them separate. The verse carefully describes arrangement and appearance without naming stones the surviving text leaves unnamed.
crossReferences: Exodus 28:17–21 — precious stones display ordered beauty in priestly service
Isaiah 54:11–12 — precious stones picture a restored dwelling established by God
Ezekiel 28:13–14 — precious stones and a holy mountain appear together
Revelation 21:19–21 — precious stones adorn the foundations of the holy city

verses.text: The seventh mountain stood in the middle of them and surpassed them in height, like the seat of a throne, and beautiful trees encircled it.
verses.study: The central mountain is both highest and throne-like, giving the landscape a royal focus. The comparison is visual: the mountain resembles a throne's seat. The surrounding trees soften the rugged mountain scene and prepare for the unique tree described next.
crossReferences: Psalm 48:1–2 — God's holy mountain is elevated and associated with royal presence
Isaiah 2:2 — the mountain of the LORD is raised above other mountains
Ezekiel 1:26 — a throne-like form appears above the heavenly expanse
Revelation 4:2–3 — the throne is surrounded by brilliant created signs

verses.text: Among them was a tree whose fragrance I had never smelled, and none among these trees had a fragrance like it; no other tree was like it. Its scent was more fragrant than every perfume. Its leaves, its blossom and its wood never wither, and its fruit was beautiful, like clusters of dates on a palm.
verses.study: The exceptional tree is known through fragrance, unfading vitality and beautiful fruit. Enoch does not name its species; the comparison concerns the fruit's clustered appearance. The description presents a life that does not decay, anticipating Michael's interpretation in the following chapter.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:9 — beautiful and fruitful trees grow in God's garden
Psalm 1:3 — the righteous are compared to a tree whose leaf does not wither
Song of Songs 7:7–8 — clustered fruit and the palm provide imagery of beauty
Ezekiel 47:12 — trees by the life-giving river bear fruit and do not wither

verses.text: Then I said, 'How beautiful and fragrant this tree is! Its leaves are lovely, and its blossom is beautiful to see.'
verses.study: Enoch responds to the tree's visible and fragrant beauty before he knows its purpose. His words remain observational, naming what the senses disclose. The meaning of the tree will come through revelation, not from beauty alone.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:9 — trees are described as pleasing to sight and good for food
Psalm 104:16 — the trees of the LORD are richly supplied
Song of Songs 2:3 — a fruitful tree is praised for shade and sweetness
Revelation 22:2 — the tree of life bears fruit and leaves connected with healing

verses.text: Then Michael, one of the holy angels who was with me and was their leader, answered me.
verses.study: Michael takes the role of interpreter at the point where observation reaches its limit. His leadership among the accompanying holy angels matches the authority of the explanation that follows in Chapter 25. The chapter closes at the threshold between seeing the tree and learning its appointed future.
crossReferences: Daniel 10:13 — Michael is named among the chief heavenly princes
Daniel 12:1 — Michael stands in a protective heavenly role
Jude 9 — Michael is identified as the archangel
Revelation 12:7 — Michael leads angels in heavenly conflict

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 24 turns from places of confinement and cosmic motion to a landscape of glory. Beyond a mountain burning day and night, Enoch sees seven precious mountains arranged around a central height that resembles the seat of a throne.

The vision joins transcendence and life. Deep ravines keep the mountains distinct, and the central mountain surpasses the others; yet beautiful trees surround the throne-like height. The most remarkable tree bears lasting leaves, blossoms and clustered fruit, and its fragrance exceeds every perfume.

The theological movement is from observation toward disclosed purpose. Enoch can describe the mountains and praise the tree's beauty, but he cannot determine its meaning by appearance. Michael's answer is reserved for Chapter 25, preserving the difference between careful witness and authorized interpretation.

The chapter's imagery resonates with biblical mountains, precious stones, thrones and life-giving trees without collapsing them into a single later symbol. Its own claim is more restrained: Enoch has reached a glorious ordered place whose central tree is unique, unfading and awaiting explanation.

crossReferences: Exodus 19:18; Deuteronomy 4:11 — a mountain burning with divine fire
Psalm 48:1–2; Isaiah 2:2 — an exalted mountain associated with divine kingship
Ezekiel 28:13–14 — precious stones and the holy mountain
Ezekiel 47:12 — unfading leaves and recurring fruit beside life-giving water
Daniel 10:13; 12:1 — Michael's leadership and heavenly role
Revelation 4:2–3; 21:19–21; 22:2 — throne, precious stones and the tree of life
